From: Samir Shah <ops@helixai.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: early sizing inputs

Hi Rafael,

We're planning to move parts of our inference traffic from Redwood's hosted API to a dedicated pool for regulatory and cost predictability. High-level numbers below — happy to fill in details on the call: 
- Steady-state: ~220 requests/minute (avg), ~18k tokens/minute
- Peak burst: up to 900 req/min for short windows (5-10m) during product events
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (~128 tokens)
- Current models: mix of 13B and 70B open models (quantized variants in tests)

Timeline: procurement wants a standing commitment and a cutover window in July.
Questions: what is the validation process you'll run before swap? How do you size the fleet (GPU type/quantity), and what cutover rehearsal cadence do you recommend?

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, HelixAI
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <ops@helixai.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted -> Dedicated migration: early sizing inputs

Samir — thanks for the numbers, this is helpful. High level we propose: 
1) Sizing workshop + quick baseline run to validate concurrency and KV cache hit rates (2 business days).
2) Staged capacity reservation (quota + warm pool) sized for steady-state + 30% burst buffer.
3) Dry-run (staging) cutover and smoke tests, then production swap during a scheduled window with rollback plan.

I'll loop in our SE and infra lead to propose concrete GPU counts and timelines. I created a placeholder mutual action plan here: https://redwood.app/mutual-action/MA-4821 — I'll populate with dates after our internal sizing call.

Proposed meeting: Tue 26 June, 10:30 PT — does that work?

- Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Samir's ask. Please see original below. Quick needs: a conservative capacity plan (GPU SKU & count), validation plan and a minimal cutover runbook we can share with Helix.

Key constraints from Helix:
- p95 latency goal: 250ms
- mix of 13B / 70B model traffic
- bursts up to ~4x steady for short windows

Initial thoughts:
- Target GPU: A800 equivalent for 70B (quantized) and A10G for 13B depending on memory/kv requirements.
- Start with concurrency profiles: 50 steady concurrent sessions, 200 peak concurrent for 10m windows.
- Reserve capacity = calculated throughput at steady concurrency + 30% buffer; have warm spare nodes for bursts.

Validation tests to run in staging:
- Throughput/latency sweep across token lengths (32/128/512)
- KV cache correctness + hit-rate measurement (prefix reuse)
- End-to-end fallbacks to hosted variants under load
- Cost-per-token estimate with different batching configs

Acceptance criteria (must pass before production swap):
- p95 latency below 250ms at steady concurrency
- no more than 2% error spike vs hosted baseline for 48h
- autoscale policies trigger within SLA in burst tests

Can each of you add a concrete sizing calc and an owner for the runbook sections? I'll coordinate with Samir for dates.

— Rafael

Adding the sizing extract and a short runbook draft. See attachment: sizing-extract-helixai.csv (excerpt below) and cutover-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook skeleton).

Sizing excerpt (rough):
- Model 13B (quantized FP4): avg tokens/min per request 140 -> avg throughput per A10G: ~180 reqs/min (conservative)
- Model 70B (4-bit): avg throughput per A800: ~60 reqs/min
- Target steady: allocate 2x A10G + 3x A800 to hit steady + 30% buffer; add 1x A800 warm spare for bursts

Smoke/dry-run plan (2-day window):
Day 1 (staging):
- Load sweep to peak burst for 30m windows
- Validate KV cache hit-rate (aim >60% for cost targets)
- Run functional regression on edge prompts
Day 2 (canary):
- Small % of production mirrored traffic into dedicated pool (traffic shadowing)
- Confirm latency/cost metrics and autoscaler behavior

Rollback triggers (examples):
- sustained p95 > 400ms for 15m
- >5% error delta vs hosted baseline

I'll attach the CSV and runbook skeleton. Karthik: need your input on autoscaler parameters (scale cooldowns, GPU spin-up assumptions). Grace: we'll need a customer communication draft for the cutover window.

Attachments in this message: sizing-extract-helixai.csv (spreadsheet excerpt), cutover-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook skeleton)

- Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Week of July 9: finalize sizing and procurement signatures
- July 16: staging dry-run (full load sweep, KV validation)
- July 23: canary swap (5% traffic mirrored to dedicated)
- July 30: production cutover window (2hr morning window, rollback plan ready)

Validation gates before 7/30: 
- 48h of staging metrics within acceptance criteria
- Successful canary (no regressions at 5% traffic)
- Procurement and SOC2 evidence shared with Marta

Operational notes: 
- We'll reserve GPUs for the committed period with a 4-week provisioning lead time. If Helix needs an earlier cutover we can accelerate but it may incur a higher procurement delta.
- Autoscaling profile: aggressive burst mode for first 10 minutes (fast scale) then conservative cooldown. Karthik will provide exact cooldown and warm-start numbers.
